50308-romney.title: Romney
50308-romney.creator: Unknown
50308-romney.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Both had qualities which raised them far above the general, and considerably higher than even the foremost of their competitors; and though preference for the work of the one or the other of them is often as much a matter of taste as of opinion, the pre-eminence of the two is beyond dispute.

62653-the-ball-of-fire.title: The Ball of Fire
62653-the-ball-of-fire.creator: George Randolph Chester
62653-the-ball-of-fire.description: A book by George Randolph Chester. A thin, wavering, treble note, so delicate that it seemed like a mere invisible cobweb of a tone, stole out of the organ loft and went pulsing up amid the dim arches. It grew in volume; it added a diapason; a deep, soft bass joined it, and then, subdued, but throbbing with the passion of a lost soul, it swelled into one of the noble preludes of Bach.

76057-london-parks-and-gardens.title: London Parks And Gardens
76057-london-parks-and-gardens.creator: Unknown
76057-london-parks-and-gardens.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. London has a peculiar fascination of its own, and to a vast number of English-speaking people all over the world it appeals with irresistible force. So much has been said and written about it that the theme might seem to be worn out, yet there are still fresh aspects to present, still hidden charms to discover, still deep problems to solve.

arxiv-1912-03410.title: Novel Approach to Infinite Products Using Multiplicative Modulus Function
arxiv-1912-03410.creator: C. Ganesa Moorthy
arxiv-1912-03410.description: Abstract . The usual nonnegative modulus function is based on addition. A natural different modulus function on the set of positive reals is introduced. Arguments for results for series through the usual modulus function are transformed to arguments for results for infinite products through the new modular function for multiplication.

arxiv-2012-13792.title: Analytical solution of SEIR model describing the free spread of the COVID-19 pandemic Journal: Chaos, Solitons and Fractals
arxiv-2012-13792.creator: Nicola Piovella
arxiv-2012-13792.description: Abstract We analytically study the SEIR (Susceptible Exposed Infectious Removed) epidemic model. The aim is to provide simple analytical expressions for the peak and asymptotic values and their characteristic times of the populations affected by the COVID-19 pandemic. 1 Introduction The COVID-19 outbreak has motivated a large number of numerical studies using epidemiology models [ 1 , 2 ] .

arxiv-2101-06845.title: Performance Analysis and Codebook Design for mmWave Beamforming System with Beam Squint
arxiv-2101-06845.creator: Hongkang Yu, Pengxin Guan, Yiru Wang, Yuping Zhao
arxiv-2101-06845.description: Abstract Beamforming technology is widely used in millimeter wave systems to combat path losses, and beamformers are usually selected from a predefined codebook. Unfortunately, the traditional codebook design neglects the beam squint effect, and this will cause severe performance degradation when the bandwidth is large.

arxiv-2112-02315.title: The Non-cutoff Vlasov-Poisson-Boltzmann and Vlasov-Poisson-Landau Systems in Union of Cubes Thanks:
arxiv-2112-02315.creator: Dingqun Deng
arxiv-2112-02315.description: Abstract . This work concerns the Vlasov-Poisson-Boltzmann system without angular cutoff and Vlasov-Poisson-Landau system including Coulomb interaction in bounded domain, namely union of cubes. We establish the global stability, exponential large-time decay with specular-reflection boundary condition when an initial datum is near Maxwellian equilibrium. We provide the compatible specular boundary condition for high-order derivatives and a velocity weighted energy estimate.

arxiv-2301-09406.title: The Reasonable Effectiveness of Diverse Evaluation Data
arxiv-2301-09406.creator: Lora Aroyo, Mark Díaz, Christopher Homan, Vinodkumar Prabhakaran, Alex Taylor, Ding Wang
arxiv-2301-09406.description: Abstract In this paper, we present findings from an semi-experimental exploration of rater diversity and its influence on safety annotations of conversations generated by humans talking to a generative AI-chat bot. We find significant differences in judgments produced by raters from different geographic regions and annotation platforms, and correlate these perspectives with demographic sub-groups.

arxiv-2306-09647.title: Environmental dependence of Type IIn supernova properties
arxiv-2306-09647.creator: Takashi J. Moriya, Lluís Galbany, Cristina Jiménez-Palau, Joseph P. Anderson, Hanindyo Kuncarayakti, Sebastián F. Sánchez, Joseph D. Lyman, Thallis Pessi, Jose L. Prieto, Christopher S. Kochanek, Subo Dong, Ping Chen
arxiv-2306-09647.description: Abstract Type IIn supernovae occur when stellar explosions are surrounded by dense hydrogen-rich circumstellar matter. The dense circumstellar matter is likely formed by extreme mass loss from their progenitors shortly before they explode. The nature of Type IIn supernova progenitors and the mass-loss mechanism forming the dense circumstellar matter are still unknown.

arxiv-2408-10428.title: Are LLMs Any Good for High-Level Synthesis? CCS: Hardware High-level and register-transfer level synthesis CCS: Computing methodologies Machine learning
arxiv-2408-10428.creator: Yuchao Liao, Tosiron Adegbija, Roman Lysecky
arxiv-2408-10428.description: Abstract . The increasing complexity and demand for faster, energy-efficient hardware designs necessitate innovative High-Level Synthesis (HLS) methodologies. This paper explores the potential of Large Language Models (LLMs) to streamline or replace the HLS process, leveraging their ability to understand natural language specifications and refactor code.

arxiv-2412-11400.title: Scaled Conjugate Gradient Method for Nonconvex Optimization in Deep Neural Networks
arxiv-2412-11400.creator: Naoki Sato naoki310303@gmail.com, Koshiro Izumi koshi-izumi@secom.co.jp, Hideaki Iiduka iiduka@cs.meiji.ac.jp
arxiv-2412-11400.description: Abstract A scaled conjugate gradient method that accelerates existing adaptive methods utilizing stochastic gradients is proposed for solving nonconvex optimization problems with deep neural networks. It is shown theoretically that, whether with constant or diminishing learning rates, the proposed method can obtain a stationary point of the problem.

arxiv-2510-20771.title: AlphaFlow: Understanding and Improving MeanFlow Models
arxiv-2510-20771.creator: Huijie Zhang, Aliaksandr Siarohin, Willi Menapace, Michael Vasilkovsky Sergey Tulyakov Qing Qu Ivan Skorokhodov
arxiv-2510-20771.description: Abstract MeanFlow has recently emerged as a powerful framework for few-step generative modeling trained from scratch, but its success is not yet fully understood. In this work, we show that the MeanFlow objective naturally decomposes into two parts: trajectory flow matching and trajectory consistency.

pmc-10524051.title: Antidepressant-induced burning mouth syndrome: A case report
pmc-10524051.creator: Alaa Alesa, Wid Kattan, Abdulhadi Albadri
pmc-10524051.description: Burning mouth syndrome is a chronic condition characterized by oral pain in the absence of intraoral clinical signs. The pathogenesis and etiology of burning mouth syndrome are not fully understood. Both men and women of all ages are at risk of developing this syndrome, but women are at an even higher risk.

pmc-10660201.title: Impact of dexmedetomidine on mortality in critically ill patients with acute kidney injury: a retrospective propensity score matching analysis
pmc-10660201.creator: Wenting Wang, Yu Jin, Peiyao Zhang, Peng Gao, He Wang, Jinping Liu
pmc-10660201.description: ObjectivesThis study sought to estimate the effect of dexmedetomidine (DEX) administration on mortality in critically ill patients with acute kidney injury (AKI).DesignA retrospective cohort study.SettingThe study sourced its data from the Multiparameter Intelligent Monitoring in Intensive Care Database IV (MIMIC-IV), a comprehensive database of intensive care unit patients.

pmc-11680431.title: How Emerging and Re-Emerging Infectious Diseases Challenge Our Understanding of Viral Infections
pmc-11680431.creator: My K Ha
pmc-11680431.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). in West Africa, the 2015 Zika virus outbreak, and the recent 2019 severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) pandemic all resulted in substantial morbidity and mortality while spreading viruses across borders to infect people in multiple countries [1,2,3]. Although medical advances, improved sanitation, and the development of novel vaccines/therapeutics have reduced overall fatality, some infectious diseases such as HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis, and malaria remain a substantial burden in developing countries due to inequalities in access to affordable healthcare [4].

pmc-13090661.title: Flexible polymeric materials and wearable biosensors for smart diabetes mellitus diagnostics and monitoring
pmc-13090661.creator: Valentine Saasa, Thandi Gumede, Nkosikhona Theoren Msweli
pmc-13090661.description: SummaryDiabetes mellitus remains a major global health challenge that requires frequent and accurate glucose monitoring. Conventional finger-prick methods are invasive and often lead to poor patient compliance. In response, flexible and wearable biosensors have emerged as promising platforms for continuous and non-invasive glucose monitoring.

pmc-13382700.title: Retention and tissue-specific expression of uncoupling protein homoeologs in Xenopus laevis
pmc-13382700.creator: Erik Rollwitz, Martin Jastroch
pmc-13382700.description: Mitochondrial uncoupling proteins (UCPs) play central roles in vertebrate energy metabolism, with UCP1 specializing as a thermogenic effector in placental mammals. Comparative genomics demonstrated that UCP1, UCP2, and UCP3 originated prior to the emergence of endothermy, suggesting that their ancestral functions evolved in ectothermic vertebrates.

pmc-13391379.title: The effect of weight-loss surgery in patients with obesity on adipose tissue mesenchymal stem cells versus circulating endothelial progenitor cells
pmc-13391379.creator: Ning Yang, Mina H Al Saeedi, Ailing Xue, Negin Mahmoudi Hamidabad, Xiangyang Zhu, Hui Tang, Kyra L Jordan, Aleksandra Kukla, Alfonso Eirin, Amir Lerman, Lilach O Lerman
pmc-13391379.description: Background/ObjectiveObesity imposes dysfunction of the endogenous cellular reparative system, which may manifest as impaired adipose tissue-derived mesenchymal stem/stromal cells (AT-MSCs) function or altered characteristics of circulating endothelial progenitor cells (EPCs). However, whether both systems are abnormal in patients with obesity remains unclear.

pmc-13574224.title: Predictors of Spontaneous Pharyngocutaneous Fistula Closure After Total Laryngectomy
pmc-13574224.creator: Ernesto Sánchez-LLanos, Rafael Fernández-Liesa, Eugenio A Vicente-González
pmc-13574224.description: Objective: This study aimed to evaluate the rate of spontaneous pharyngocutaneous fistula (PCF) closure after total laryngectomy and to identify clinical, inflammatory, radiotherapy-related, and perioperative factors associated with successful conservative management.Materials and methods: A retrospective observational study was conducted, including patients who underwent total laryngectomy between 2010 and 2025. Clinical, surgical, and oncological variables were collected from medical records.

pmc-13594503.title: Benzothiazepane‐Based Curcumin Analogs Show Selective Effects on Respiration, Permeability, and Growth of Gut‐Liver (Co‐Culture) Cell Models
pmc-13594503.creator: Fuhua Li, Julie De Munck, Felien Morlion, Katarina Magdalenic, Andreja Rajkovic, Matthias D'hooghe, John Van Camp, Charlotte Grootaert
pmc-13594503.description: Curcumin, a natural polyphenol with anti‐cancer potential, faces limitations due to metabolic instability, and non‐specific toxicity. This study focused on four curcumin analogs (FM038, FM044, FM045, FM050) featuring oxobutenylidene‐substituted benzothiazepane cores bearing pyridinyl or furan substituents. We systematically evaluated their selective toxic effect on human colon (Caco‐2) and liver (HepG2) cells.
